name: Muslim Law & Jurisprudence
summary: 49 descriptive questions extracted · 16 topic groups · Years represented: 2016, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2024, 2025
officialReference: Official syllabus reference: printed pages 113–114 of the FPSC revised syllabus.
frequentTopics: Most frequent mapped topics: Integrated / Cross-Syllabus Questions (13) · Islamic Family Law (7) · Marriage (5) · Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 (4) · Islamic Criminal Law (3) · Islamic Law of Contract (3)

questions.text: Explain the primary sources of Islamic law and their significance in contemporary (20) jurisprudence.

The four Sunni canonical schools hold Ijmāʻ to be a valid source of law. But it is said (20) that “there is no workable machinery for the selection of qualified jurists to take part in Ijmāʻ and for establishing their deliberations in an authoritative form”. Discuss and give arguments for and against this opinion.

How the classical Muslim jurists defined riba when, unlike many of the contemporary (20) scholars, they did not distinguish between the riba of the Qur’an and the riba of the Sunnah? Explain the implications of considering riba a mujmal (unelaborated) term of the Qur’an, which has been elaborated by the Prophetic traditions.
Define Sunnah and explain the inseparable bond of the Sunnah with the Qur’an by (20) highlighting in particular how the Sunnah elaborates the meaning of the Qur’an.
(a) What are the rational sources of Islamic law? (7) (b) What are the elements of Qiyas? (7) (c) Explain Qiyas with the help of an example. (6)

Write short notes on any TWO of the following: (10 marks each) (20) (a) Imam Shafi’I as the master-architect of Islamic jurisprudence. (b) Meaning and scope of ijtihad (c) Implications of positive command (amr) and negative command (nahy) for various legal rules.

Imām Shāfiʻī studied deeply the principles of Ḥanafī school of law. He disagreed with (20) some views of Ḥanafī jurists and established his own independent school. What were his differences with Ḥanafīs and what did he contribute in modification of Islamic law and jurisprudence?
How crimes can be classified in Islamic criminal law on the basis of right effected? (20) Elaborate your answer in the light of classical Muslim jurists.

“For you, there is life in qisas.”(Qur’an, 2:179). Elaborate the implications of this (20) Divine Injunction in the light of the various theories of punishment, such as retribution, deterrence, reformation and prevention.
‘Islamic criminal law appears to be harsh, but a closer look reveals that in practice the (20) most severe punishments are hardly ever applied.’ Discuss.

topics.title: Marriage
analysis: Pattern: Critical/analytical command words are less common in the later part of the supplied series (0% vs 50%).

questions.text: Explain the concept of 'Nikah' and the essential requirements for a valid Muslim (20) marriage.
Write down the difference between Khul‘a and dissolution of marriage in the (20) perspective of Shari'a and conventional law.
What is meant by a fāsīd (irregular) marriage? What are the legal effects of such (20) marriage? How an irregular marriage can be validated?

Discuss critically the admissibility of inserting stipulations in a marriage contract by (20) the parties. Your answer should be based on the debates of classical Muslim jurists and modern scholars. Your own opinion is also required.
Discuss the extent to which a normal marriage contract can be varied to benefit women (20) under Islamic law.

topics.title: Islamic Family Law

questions.text: What is the Islamic perspective on trade and commerce? How does Islamic law (20) regulate business practices?
Discuss the rights and responsibilities of spouses under Islamic family law. (20)
What is the concept of 'Tawbah' (repentance) in Islamic law? How does it relate to (20) the forgiveness of crimes?
What is meant by ikrāh in Islamic law? Explain that how ikrāh effects a free will? (20) What are the various opinions of the Muslim jurists regarding the effect of ikrāh on a free will?
Does Islamic law distinguish between the consequences of direct and indirect (20) participation in hostilities? Also explain what rules and principles of Islamic law are violated by suicide attacks.
Is the Qur’an a code of Islamic law? Discuss. (20)
Discuss the natural causes of defective legal capacity in Islamic law. (20)

Write short notes on the following: (5 each) (20) (a) Triple talaq in one sitting (b) Remedies available to a Muslim women under the DMMA 1939 (c) Dower (d) Share of the grandchild under the MFLO 1961
Explain the procedure of Talaq-e-Ahsan and Talaq-e-Hassan.

topics.title: Islamic Law of Contract
analysis: Appearances: 3  |  Years: 2016, 2017, 2024  |  Demands: Critically examine (1), Evaluate/Assess (1), Explain/Elucidate (1)

questions.text: Write down “Contract Writing Standards” in the context of Conventional and (20) Islamic law.
Define ʻAqd’ according to Muslim jurists. Which are the circumstances that affect the (20) legal capacity of the parties to execute a contract under Islamic Sharīʻah?
Explain and critically evaluate the main restrictions imposed in Islamic law on the (20) freedom of contract.
Discuss the principles of Islamic banking and insurance. How do they differ from (20) conventional systems?
Discuss origin and development of Islamic law of International relations? (20)
Review the implementation of fundamental human rights in the context of Islam (20) and International Humanitarian Law (IHL).
Discuss the relationship between Maqasid-e-Shariah and Human Rights. (20)

Elaborate how the issue of apostasy of Muslim women in British India prompted the (20) Hanafi scholars to find solutions for the problems of married women in the Maliki School and how their efforts culminated in the form of Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939. Also explain reasons for this Act’s becoming almost redundant in Pakistan.

questions.text: Discuss whether the laws revealed previously to the promulgation of Islam are binding (20) on the Muslims or not?

Explain the provisions of Section 4, Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, about the (20) right of inheritance for the orphaned grandchildren. Evaluate the arguments for and against this law from the perspective of repugnancy with Islamic Injunctions.
Does Islam allow privatization of law? Discuss in the light of Blasphemy laws of Pakistan.

Write notes on the following topics: (5 marks each) (20) (A) Analysis of the terminology Uṣūl al-fiqh (B) Status of mutawatir tradition (C) Ṭalāq rajʻī and its rules (D) Section 4 of Muslim Family Law Ordinance 1961

questions.text: Discuss the Islamic legal framework surrounding the protection of personal (20) property and wealth.
Explain the difference between ‘Illat and Ḥikmat in the context of Qiyās (analogy) (20) and write down the conditions of Aṣal and ‘Illat.
Explain the concept of Ijtihad by Allama Iqbal and the role of contemporary (20) institutions engaged in this regard.
Write down the conditions of acceptance of Khabar Wāḥid. Give the opinion of (20) Aḥnāf and Mālikiya.
Explain the meaning of Dalalat-un-Nas and their contemporary arguments. (20)
Discuss those circumstances which impair legal capacity of a person and prevent him (20) from concluding contacts and making disposition in his property.
What is meant by Diminishing Mushārakha? Discuss how the contemporary Islamic (20) banks use such type of transaction for house financing?
Write notes on any TWO of the following: (10 marks each) (20) (a) The conditions of obligation(taklīf). (b) Legal capacity (c) Kinds of capacity for acquisition
Differentiate between following terms/concepts: (5 each) (a) Fiqh and Shariah (b) Ijtihad and Taqleed (c) Wajib and Fard (d) Hukm-e-taklifi and Hukum-e-wadi
Discuss any two of the following transactions: (10 each) (a) Mudarba (b) Murabaha (c) Ijarah

Give your peer analysis about the approaches of Al-Ghazālī and Al-Shāṭibī on the (20) doctrine of maqāṣid al-Sharīʻah. Explore the primary and secondary purposes of this doctrine and discuss whether maqāṣid al-Sharīʻah are definite in number as determined by the earlier jurists or they may be increased.

Muslim jurists classified offences on the basis of right. Why was there need of this (20) classification? What important consequences flow from it and what will be the result if this classification is changed?
What are conditions for exercising universal ijtihad? Discuss the role of ijtihad today. (20)
